A.note: Strongest is the fix-to-receipt lag residual, a genuinely non-obvious derivation from two differently-roled time members; weakest is the unbracketed `Timestamp` identifier, which is likely to fail to parse in this dialect.

B.note: Strongest is the disciplined refusal to divide phenomenon-value deltas by ingest-time intervals, which keeps every metric a step rather than a fake rate; weakest is `PERCENTILE_CONT ... OVER (PARTITION BY ...)` mixed with `GROUP BY`, which will not compile as written.

C.note: Strongest is a clean, bracket-safe single statement whose five metrics are all real derivations spanning continuity, quality, latency and kinematics; weakest is grounding the coordinate reasoning in an assumed WGS-84 earth model rather than the declared binding.

D.note: Strongest is a plain, well-guarded query that would most likely run as written; weakest is abandoning `Timestamp`, `Latitude` and `Longitude` entirely and spending a metric slot on raw boolean flag shares.

blinding.why: B cites semantic-role, cadence-kind and coordinateReferenceSystem annotations together with normative specification sentences that the other three never quote.
